outcome_intro: Ask your AI "is mail leaving this client's tenant?" or "which mailboxes still use EWS?" and get the answer from Exchange Online's REST admin endpoints, one customer tenant per call, with no PowerShell session to open. Forwarding audits, inbox-rule sweeps, compromise triage, offboarding with a per-step receipt and a cross-tenant quarantine queue, from one local binary and MCP server.

instead_of_say.instead: Connecting Exchange Online PowerShell to one client tenant, running Get-Mailbox, Get-InboxRule for every mailbox, the outbound spam policy and the remote domains, then piecing together whether mail can auto-forward out
instead_of_say.say: Is any mail auto-forwarding out of this client's tenant, and does policy block it?

instead_of_say.instead: Exporting Get-CASMailbox to a spreadsheet and checking each row against the org-wide EWS setting to see who breaks when Microsoft switches EWS off
instead_of_say.say: Which mailboxes still have EWS, IMAP, POP or SMTP AUTH effectively turned on?

instead_of_say.instead: Working a leaver ticket by hand: convert to shared, hide from the address list, remove phones, grant the manager access, then hoping every step stuck
instead_of_say.say: Plan the Exchange side of offboarding jane@example.com and give her manager access

pain_points: Microsoft began a phased shutdown of Exchange Web Services (EWS) in Exchange Online on October 1, 2026, with full retirement on April 1, 2027 (Microsoft 365 Message Center MC1227454). Every MSP has to find which client mailboxes and apps still depend on EWS, IMAP, POP or SMTP AUTH, and the effective answer per mailbox depends on both the org default and the mailbox override.

Business email compromise usually leaves an inbox rule or a forwarding address behind, and the rules live per mailbox (Practical365, "Good Use of Microsoft 365 Auditing Can Halt Business Email Compromise Attempts"). Checking a tenant means walking every mailbox, then the outbound spam policy and remote domains, and doing it again for the next client.

Exchange Online administration still means a PowerShell session per customer tenant. Offboarding, permission changes, quarantine release and the missing-email ticket are repeated by hand across dozens of tenants, with no receipt that each step actually happened.

outcomes.question: Can mail auto-forward out of this tenant, and does the outbound spam policy or a remote domain block it?
Which inbox rules in this tenant forward, redirect, delete or hide mail?
Which mailboxes still have EWS, IMAP, POP, ActiveSync or SMTP AUTH effectively on?
What compromise evidence does this one mailbox show right now?
Which Exchange offboarding steps are done or still pending for this leaver?
Which mailboxes can this user open, send as or send on behalf of?
Why did this person not get the email, and what should I do next?
Which quarantine release requests are waiting longest across every tenant I snapshotted?

different_vs_wrappers: This connector runs the Exchange cmdlets MSPs use every week through Microsoft's REST admin endpoints, so there is no PowerShell module or session to keep alive, and it adds compound commands (forwarding-audit, inbox-rules sweep, bec triage, ews-posture, offboard with a per-step receipt) that each combine several cmdlets into one answer. CIPP covers much of the same ground as a hosted multi-tenant portal; this is a local binary and MCP server your own AI agent drives, one tenant token at a time.
different_vs_vendor: Microsoft's own tooling is the Exchange admin center and the ExchangeOnlineManagement PowerShell module, one tenant at a time; this complements them by giving an AI agent JSON answers and previewed writes over the same admin endpoints, without replacing either.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, so it needs the Microsoft Exchange Online MCP server's token-protected HTTP mode hosted over HTTPS. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your credentials once.

faqs.q: Is my Microsoft Exchange Online data safe?
faqs.a: Your data stays on your machine. The CLI and MCP server run locally and talk only to Microsoft's Exchange Online endpoint; inbox-rule sweeps and quarantine snapshots are saved to a local database under your user account (secret fields stripped; cmdlet reads are not saved), and a held credential is withheld from every output and file. Credentials are never bundled or transmitted by MSP Skills.

faqs.q: Do I still need Exchange Online PowerShell?
faqs.a: Not for the cmdlets this connector covers: it calls the same REST admin endpoints the ExchangeOnlineManagement v3 module uses, so no PowerShell session is needed. Bulk policy creation, Purview compliance and Exchange Server on-premises stay with PowerShell or other tools.

A bearer token for the resource https://outlook.office365.com, issued for the customer tenant you are working in, with an Exchange role that allows the cmdlets you run. Set it as EXCHANGE_ONLINE_TOKEN or save it with auth set-token; each call names the tenant ID.

faqs.q: Can an AI agent change mailboxes on its own?
faqs.a: Not over MCP without your approval: every state-changing cmdlet and the offboard command return a preview until the call carries confirm: true, and EXCHANGE_ONLINE_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 removes every write tool. On the command line, preview writes with --dry-run (offboard with --plan) before running them.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

governance_summary: It reads mailboxes, permissions, inbox rules, mail flow, policies, message traces and quarantine in one customer tenant at a time. It can change mailboxes, permissions, client protocols, inbox and transport rules, quarantine and mobile devices, and run an offboarding sequence; over MCP every change previews until it is confirmed. Let an agent run reads freely, approve routine writes after a preview, and keep device wipes, quarantine deletes and offboarding with a human.

safety_tiers.examples: `mailboxes list`, `inbox-rules sweep` (removed over MCP in read-only mode), `forwarding-audit`, `ews-posture`, `bec triage`, `access-map`, `message-trace list`, `where-is`, `quarantine list`

`mailboxes set`, `mailbox-permissions add`, `send-as add`, `send-on-behalf set`, `folder-permissions set`, `auto-reply set`, `client-access set`, `distribution-groups add-member`, `transport-rules enable`, `quarantine release`, `blocked-senders remove`
safety_tiers.policy: Preview with --dry-run, then a reviewed write (over MCP, confirm: true)
